p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram shows the processes and materials involved in a DNA microarray experiment. The diagram begins at the top with illustrations of a fertilized egg on the left and a tadpole on the right. The fertilized egg is a small brown oval structure, cross-sectioned, with a small yellow dot in the center. The tadpole, to the right, is small and brown and facing to the right. Both are labeled above. To the left there is a gray text box reading, “Isolate mRNAs from cells at two stages of development; each mRNA sample represents all the genes expressed in the cells at that stage.” Below is a down arrow from the tadpole and from the egg, each pointing to a mass of dark green snippets of mRNA (labeled left). Below each, there is a down arrow. To the left is a gray text box reading, “Convert mRNAs to cDNAs with reverse transcriptase, using fluorescently labeled deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates.” The left arrow, from the egg, points down to a light green, glowing mass of cDNA (labeled left); the right arrow, from the tadpole, points down to a red, glowing mass of cDNA. Two arrows pointing down from these images merge into a single arrow, which points down to a DNA microarray (labeled above), which is a gray square structure with about 90 wells (gray circles) on it. To the left is a text box reading, “Allow fluorescent cDNAs to anneal to complementary sequences on the microarray.” Below is a down arrow with a text box on the left reading, “Each fluorescent spot represents a gene expressed in the cells.” On the right of the arrow is text reading, “removal of unhybridized cDNAs.” Below there is a DNA microarray that is black with glowing green, red, and yellow wells. A yellow glowing well is pointed out on the right and has text reading, “Unchanged expression (yellow).” A green well is pointed out on the left and has text reading, “Higher expression at single-cells stage (green).” A red well points out on the left and has text reading, “Higher expression at tadpole stage (red).”
